class.name: GroundSurface3D
class.brief_description: Footprints, ruts and dents in sand, soil, mud and leaf litter.
class.description: A field of dents and rims around the camera over bare ground. Nodes in [member deform_groups] press it: loaded bodies sink by Bekker's pressure-sinkage relation with Wong's soil values ([i]Theory of Ground Vehicles[/i]), the pressed material is partly compacted and partly pushed into a rim so volume is kept, and walls steeper than the material's angle of repose slump down (Sumner, O'Brien and Hodgins 1999, "Animating Sand, Mud, and Snow"). What the ground is made of follows rules per place: [member ground_type] (or [member type_map]) gives sand or soil; the moisture ([member moisture], or the [code]WeatherMap3D[/code] wetness) turns soil to mud and dry sand to damp sand, so a boot sinks 2 cm in dry sand, under 1 cm in damp sand and about 8 cm in mud, dry sand prints cave in to dishes, damp ones keep sharp walls and mud creeps back over minutes; tree crowns (the weather map's canopy closure) drop [member litter_depth] of leaf litter; bare rock from a [code]TerrainGenerator3D[/code] height source does not print, nor does ground under a [code]SnowCover3D[/code] pack. Freshly turned ground is darker until it dries ([member drying_time]); wind fills dry sand prints and rain softens them. The node draws the field as a patch with [member material], the terrain's own material, and the terrain drawn with that material (with [member BaseMaterial3D.ground_deform_enabled], or [method BaseMaterial3D.get_ground_deform_shader_code] in a shader) is lowered under the patch by [member skirt], so the prints are geometry in raster and under path tracing. Bodies keep standing on the terrain's own collider; [method get_surface_height_at] gives the printed surface for foot placement.

method.name: bed_load
method.description: The bed load of fine sand (0.25 mm) under water flowing at [param water_speed] m/s (depth-averaged), m² per second per metre across the flow: Meyer-Peter and Mueller (1948). [code]0.0[/code] under the Shields threshold, about 0.25 m/s.

method.name: clear_deformation
method.description: Removes every print, including the cached tiles.

method.name: deposit
method.description: Lays [param depth] m of sand over a disc of [param radius] at [param position] (a hollow there fills first). The volume is the disc's exactly, also for a disc smaller than a cell. Returns it, m3 ([code]0[/code] off soft ground). For grains landing ([PhysXGroundGrains3D]).

method.name: dig
method.description: Takes [param depth] m of sand out of a disc of [param radius] at [param position], any rim there first. Returns the volume, m3 ([code]0[/code] off soft ground). For grains leaving the ground ([PhysXGroundGrains3D]).

method.name: get_cached_tile_count
method.description: The number of tiles of prints kept for when the field comes back over them.

method.name: get_deform_rect
method.description: The field's world XZ rectangle.

method.name: get_dent_at
method.description: How far the ground at [param position] is pressed below its undisturbed height, in metres.

method.name: get_footing_at
method.description: The footing at [param position] for a walker of [param mass] kg on [param area] m² of boot: [code]soft[/code], [code]sinkage[/code] (m), [code]effort[/code] (the work of walking against firm ground, 2.1 on dry sand), [code]speed_scale[/code] (its inverse) and [code]slide[/code] (an acceleration down a face steeper than the material holds, m/s²). The game decides how a controller uses them.

method.name: get_fresh_at
method.description: How freshly turned the ground at [param position] is, from 1 (just dug) to 0 (dried).

method.name: get_ground_height_at
method.description: The undisturbed ground height at [param position], from the height source.

method.name: get_material_at
method.description: The rules at [param position]: [code]n[/code], [code]kc[/code], [code]kphi[/code] (Bekker), [code]rim_share[/code], [code]repose[/code] (degrees), [code]rate[/code] (slumping share per second), [code]max_dent[/code], [code]litter[/code] (m), [code]sand[/code] (share), [code]blown[/code] (the share the wind moves: dry, bare sand) and [code]deformable[/code].

method.name: get_moved_volume
method.description: The volume pressed down (x) and piled into rims (y) over the live field, in m³. Their difference is what was compacted.

method.name: get_patch_material
method.description: The copy of [member material] the patch is drawn with.

method.name: get_rim_at
method.description: How much material is piled on the ground at [param position], in metres.

method.name: get_ripple_at
method.description: The wind ripple height at [param position] over the ripple layer's mean, in metres; [code]0.0[/code] outside the ripple window or with [member wind_ripples] off.

method.name: get_ripple_cell
method.description: The ripple layer's cell size in metres: [member detail_spacing] divided down to about 1.25 cm, so the patch's fine vertices sit on its cells.

method.name: get_ripple_heights
method.description: The ripple layer's heights, [method get_ripple_size] squared, row by row along Z from [method get_ripple_origin]. For tests and tools.

method.name: get_ripple_origin
method.description: The world XZ of the ripple window's corner, in metres.

method.name: get_ripple_size
method.description: The ripple window's width in cells (it spans [member ripple_extent]).

method.name: get_ripple_steps
method.description: How many saltation steps the ripples have taken since [member wind_ripples] was turned on, not counting the field grown in the background.

method.name: get_saturation_at
method.description: The pore water in the top 2 cm of the ground at [param position], as a share of the pore space (0 dry, 1 saturated). See [member water_coupling].

method.name: get_sinkage_at
method.description: How far a body of [param mass] kg on [param area] m² ([param width] m wide, 0: from the area) sinks into the ground at [param position], in metres.

method.name: get_step_time_msec
method.description: The time the last physics step took (pressing, slumping, ageing, upload), in milliseconds.

method.name: get_surface_height_at
method.description: The printed ground height at [param position]: the undisturbed ground plus the rim minus the dent.

method.name: get_water_speed_at
method.description: The speed of the water flowing over the ground at [param position], m/s; [code]0.0[/code] where it is dry.

method.name: get_water_step_usec
method.description: How long the last water step took, in microseconds (it runs twice a second).

method.name: get_wheel_soil
method.description: The soil under a wheel at [param position]: [param load] N on a wheel of [param radius] and [param width] m, a tyre at [param inflation] kPa ([code]0[/code]: rigid), at [param slip] and [param slip_angle] (radians). Returns [code]soft[/code], [code]static_sinkage[/code], [code]sinkage[/code] (m, with slip sinkage), [code]contact_length[/code] (m), [code]compaction[/code], [code]bulldozing[/code], [code]resistance[/code], [code]shear_limit[/code], [code]traction[/code] and [code]lateral[/code] (N).

method.name: is_gpu_active
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when the field runs in compute shaders: [member gpu_simulation] is on and there is a [RenderingDevice] (Forward+ or Mobile).

method.name: is_ripples_ready
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] once the first ripple field grown in the background has filled the window.

method.name: press
method.description: Presses the ground down to [param bottom] (world height) under a sphere of [param radius] at [param position] ([param round]) or a flat disc, plus [param sink] below the undisturbed surface. Returns the volume moved, in m³.

method.name: press_box
method.description: Presses a flat print [param size] wide (x) and long (z), turned by [param yaw] about up: a boot, a crate. Returns the volume moved, in m³.

method.name: press_wheel
method.description: Presses a wheel's rut: a flat print [param size] wide (x) and long (z), turned by [param yaw], [param sinkage] m deep, the soil thrown along [param velocity]. Returns the volume moved on the CPU field ([code]0[/code] on the GPU, where it is a stamp).

method.name: refresh_ground
method.description: Samples the height source again (after the terrain changed).

method.name: settle
method.description: Runs slumping and ageing for [param seconds] at once, in steps of [param step].

method.name: sync_deformation
method.description: On the GPU path, waits for the field and reads it back now, so [method get_dent_at], [method get_rim_at], [method get_fresh_at], [method get_surface_height_at] and [method get_moved_volume] show everything pressed so far. It stalls the GPU: for tests and tools, not every frame. Does nothing on the CPU path.

method.name: take_sprays
method.description: The sand thrown by spinning wheels since the last call (from [PhysXVehicle3D] on soft soil), as Dictionaries: [code]position[/code], [code]velocity[/code], [code]width[/code], [code]slip_speed[/code], [code]reach_center[/code] and [code]reach_radius[/code] (the loose sand the tread reaches). Taken by a [PhysXGroundGrains3D]; with none, they are dropped after a couple of physics frames.

members.member: The contact area of a [CharacterBody3D] in [member deform_groups] without a [code]ground_contact_area[/code] meta, in m² (one boot by default).
The mass of a [CharacterBody3D] in [member deform_groups] without a [code]ground_mass[/code] meta, in kg.
How close a body's underside must come to the surface to press it, in metres.
The width of the field, in metres. Prints are made only where the terrain is fully lowered: [member terrain_margin] plus [member skirt_fade] inside its edge.

Groups whose nodes press the ground. A node's first collision shape gives its footprint; rigid bodies press by their mass, characters by [member character_mass], others only to their underside. The metas [code]ground_mass[/code], [code]ground_contact_area[/code] and [code]ground_radius[/code] (or the snow ones) override.
Texels across the field (a multiple of 64).
The patch's vertex spacing over the middle half of the field, in metres.
How long freshly turned ground takes to dry to a third of its darkening, in seconds.
The node the field follows; the camera when empty.

Runs the field (pressing, slumping, ageing, the turned-ground tint and the tile cache) in compute shaders where there is a [RenderingDevice]; the texture the ground materials sample is written there directly. The queries use a copy read back at 15 Hz. Off, or on the Compatibility renderer, the field runs on the CPU. Turning it over starts the field empty.
The physics layers a downward ray finds the ground on when [member height_source] gives no height.
The spacing of the ground lattice sampled from the height source, in metres.
The ground where [member type_map] says nothing: sand or soil.

The terrain: a [code]TerrainDeformer3D[/code], a baked [code]TerrainDataMap3D[/code], a [code]TerrainGenerator3D[/code], anything with [code]get_height(position)[/code] or Terrain3D. Empty: a downward ray on [member ground_collision_mask].
The canopy closure that drops leaf litter when there is no weather map, from 0 to 1.
The leaf litter under a closed canopy, in metres; less under a thinner one.

The terrain's material. The patch is drawn with a copy of it; turn on [member BaseMaterial3D.ground_deform_enabled] on the original (or call the shader code from a [ShaderMaterial]) so the terrain is lowered under the patch. Map it by world position so the two line up.
How many tiles of prints are kept after the field leaves them.
The ground's moisture from 0 (dry) to 1 (soaked); -1 takes the [code]WeatherMap3D[/code] wetness.
The patch's vertex spacing over the outer half of the field, in metres.
Rigid bodies in [member deform_groups] moving through soft ground feel its resistance: compaction and bulldozing of the soil they move into, at their width.
How fast rain softens prints: the share lost per hour per mm/h of rain.

Width of the square of real ripple geometry round the follow point, m. The patch's middle is meshed at the ripple cell over it, so its vertex count grows as its square (4 m: about 100,000 vertices). The ripples fade out over its outer 15%, into the same field drawn as surface detail (a normal, no shadows of their own) over the rest of the patch.
Speeds up the ripples' growth over real time; [code]1.0[/code] is real time, when ripples take minutes to re-form. For scenes and time-lapses.
If [code]true[/code] and the height source is a [code]TerrainGenerator3D[/code], bare rock (exposure over one half) does not print.
How fast wind fills dry sand prints: the share lost per hour at 10 m/s, from nothing at 5 m/s (Bagnold's threshold).
How far the terrain is lowered under the patch, in metres.
Over how many metres the lowering reaches its full depth, past [member terrain_margin].
A [code]SnowCover3D[/code]: where it has more than 3 cm of snow, the snow surface takes the print instead.
How far inside the field's edge the terrain starts to be lowered, in metres; at least the terrain's vertex spacing, so no lowered triangle reaches past the patch.
A map of the ground over [member type_map_rect]: red is the share of sand, green over one half is bare rock.
The world XZ rectangle [member type_map] covers.

If [code]true[/code], water over the ground changes it. Water from [member water_sources] and the [code]WeatherMap3D[/code] contact wetness fills the pores of the top layer (saturated in about 10 s under water), which drain to field capacity in a minute or two and dry over hours. Damp sand is firm and holds steep walls; saturated sand slumps as dry sand does. Water flowing faster than the Shields threshold (about 0.25 m/s) moves the sand ([method bed_load]): prints under the swash or a stream are rounded off within a minute, the volume kept. The pore water also shows: wet sand darkens and turns smoother (Lagarde's porous wet surfaces), and a film stands glossy on saturated sand and under the water, in raster and under the path tracer alike, through the [code]ground_wet_map[/code] shader global.

The water nodes the ground reads, sampled on a 1 m grid twice a second: any node with [code]sample_depth(position)[/code] (or [code]sample_height(position)[/code]), [code]sample_flow(position)[/code] and, for a sea's swash, [code]sample_swash(position)[/code], such as the water surface, river and live water nodes.
The 10 m wind over the ground in m/s, as world XZ. [code]Vector2(0, 0)[/code] reads it from the [code]WeatherMap3D[/code].

If [code]true[/code], wind over dry sand grows ripples (Nishimori and Ouchi 1993) over [member ripple_extent] round the follow point: about 11 cm apart and 6 mm high at 8 m/s, crests across the wind, none under about 6 m/s (Bagnold's threshold), on damp sand or under litter (damp sand keeps the ripples it has). Prints wipe them and they grow back; a wind shift turns them. The patch's middle is meshed at the ripple cell, so the crests are real geometry the path tracer sees. [GroundStreamers3D] draws the grains in the air. Off by default until its cost is measured.

constants.constant: Sand: dry it caves in to dishes, damp it keeps sharp walls.
Soil: firm when dry, mud when wet.
